exercise.name: Glute Bridge

reference.title: Glute Bridge Two Legs on Floor (female)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip extension; knees and feet fixed)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive the hips up, keep breathing in the squeeze, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, 1 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Longer squeeze, then single-leg bridge, then hip thrust from a bench

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width, arms on the floor by your sides.
Breathe out, press through the heels and drive the hips up.
Knees, hips and shoulders in one line. Squeeze the glutes; ribs down, no arching.
Breathe in and lower the hips slowly back to the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop when knees, hips and shoulders line up; tuck the pelvis slightly and keep the ribs down.
Keep the knees over the feet, hip width apart.

mistakes.mistake: Feeling it mostly in the hamstrings (cramping)
mistakes.fix: Bring the feet a little closer to the hips; more knee bend lowered hamstring activity in Lehecka 2017.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing through the neck or head
mistakes.fix: Weight on the upper back and feet; neck relaxed, chin gently tucked.

kinematics.norm: Hips extend to neutral at the top (straight knee-hip-shoulder line); no extra lumbar arch (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the top is the traditional bridge; more knee bend shifts work away from the hamstrings (Lehecka 2017)
Shoulder-to-hip line rises until it is in line with the thighs (clinical opinion)
Pelvis lifts until the line is straight (clinical opinion)
Controlled: about 1-2 s up, a brief squeeze, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #247112, Glute Bridge Two Legs on Floor (female), video (movement reference)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace the abdomen first.
Hamstring cramps: move the feet closer to the hips.
regressions: Smaller lift (pelvic tilt to a half bridge).
progressions: Hip thrust with the upper back on a bench.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor lifting the pelvis. Cueing the glutes about doubled gluteus maximus activity in a bridge study listed by Macadam 2019 (16.8% to 33.0% MVIC).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor lifting the pelvis. Cueing the glutes about doubled gluteus maximus activity in a bridge study listed by Macadam 2019 (16.8% to 33.0% MVIC).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; with the knees at about 90 degrees they work hard. Biceps femoris reached about 75% MVIC in a single-leg bridge at 90 degrees of knee flexion (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; with the knees at about 90 degrees they work hard. Biceps femoris reached about 75% MVIC in a single-leg bridge at 90 degrees of knee flexion (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and keeps the knees from drifting apart (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and keeps the knees from drifting apart (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the knees in line with the feet; it was active in bridging studies (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the knees in line with the feet; it was active in bridging studies (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the knee angle and press the feet into the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the knee angle and press the feet into the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the ribs down and the pelvis neutral so the lift comes from the hips, not the low back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk in line; they should not take over by arching the low back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk in line; they should not take over by arching the low back (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Hip extended to neutral at the top
